profile.headline: Engineer | Java, R, Spatial Statistics
profile.summary:
I am a versatile and innate problem solver and a learner, a coding and math enthusiast, and a succinct and direct communicator.  With my professional experience and my formal education as an engineer along with my deep interest and skills in software eng., I bring together passion for (1) the development of tools that will make a positive impact on our community and on the general public and (2) projects that leverage computing and statistics to address questions that advance applied knowledge that benefits society.

I bring experience in varied fields including high-performance computing, spatial statistics, modeling, water engineering, and molecular dynamics. I am familiar with a variety of programming languages, including Java, R, C++, and Python, and I am consistently adding skills to my portfolio.

positions.title: Environmental Engineer
positions.description:
Reduced modeling post-processing times by 90%+ by developing software tools (mostly R and Python) that streamlined, optimized, and simplified data-intensive processes.

Improved accuracy and reduced data needs of forecasts of water systems, including the largest reservoir in the US, by developing statistical models that ran in parallel to existing mechanistic models.

Identified, fixed, and reported bugs in modeling software from other developers and provided feedback to ensure best practices in the future in multiple languages, including unfamiliar ones (to me) such as Fortran.

Informed regulation evolution and attainment and supported management and development of water systems. I did this via computational modeling rooted in a sound understanding of complex systems with large databases aided by the production of insightful statistical reviews and adequate spatial/temporal visualizations.

positions.title: PhD Candidate/Research Assistant
positions.description:
Quantified the effect of climate change and mountain pine beetle infestations on the water quality of the streams in the Rocky Mountains at an unprecedented scale in scientific literature. I achieved this by compiling and processing big data via supercomputing, performing rigorous statistical data analyses, and applying environmental science concepts and principles.

Developed a method that merges multiple categorical images/rasters/maps into a single product with adjustable resolution while estimating the distributed uncertainty in each pixel and timestep. This is an unparalleled methodology because other existing methodologies either cannot deal with categorical data and/or with mismatched/misaligned input resolution/lattices/grids. I accomplished this by combining spatial statistics and parallel computing and by effective communication with experts in those fields.

I published a publicly available and high-resolution land cover product of the Rocky Mountains (http://hdl.handle.net/11124/170731). The detail in categorization and refined timestep of the maps is unmatched by other publicly available products. I developed this product by implementing the prior methodology with high-performance computing.

Executed the largest (scalability-wise) simulation in the history of the supercomputer of Colorado School of Mines (as of 2017). This simulation scaled almost linearly as input grew until reaching the full capacity of the supercomputer (128 nodes, 2,048 processors). I attained this level of efficiency in parallelism by maintaining awareness of the core notions behind parallelism (MPI, specifically) during the software development of the aforementioned methodology.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant and Instructor of Subsurface Contaminant Transport
positions.description:
Prepared and delivered insightful and applied lectures for a class of 25 graduate students in groundwater modeling. Taught methods for using state-of-the-art numerical methods in common commercially available software (e.g, MS Excel).

Achieved high student satisfaction (98%) through providing ample and flexible office hours to help students overcome obstacles in their learning process, developing adequate assignments, and grading with detailed insights which improved student engagement and learning.

positions.title: Intern in Parallel Computational Sciences (SIParCS)
positions.description:
Supported enhanced compression (50%+) of climate model outputs by developing an automated tool to select appropriate lossy compression based on geospatial properties of output variables. The tool executed efficiently (~linear scalability) in the Yellowstone supercomputer and supported the overarching goal of "Accelerating Statistical Analysis through Parallel Computations".

Bolstered other aspects of the climate models output compression optimization project by collaborating with other scientists, engineers, and interns from the Institute for Mathematics Applied to Geosciences (IMAGe) and other departments. I collaborated with the IMAGe team in the writing of manuscripts and proposals, reviewing code developed by other developers and providing feedback, and enhancement of existing documentation of R packages developed in IMAGe.

company.name: NCAR - The National Center for Atmospheric Research

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Developed a modeling tool to simulate the water quality of an urban basin that integrated the drainage system and the streams in the city of Bogotá in order to provide optimal operations and suitable expansion recommendations for the Water and Sewage Company of Bogota. 

Supported the improvement of the Bogotá River water quality and urban public health by designing an affordable treatment plant for a tannery to comply with standards while accounting for their finances and production level. This included gaining a deep understanding of the socio-economic and industrial factors affecting the region through the performance of field campaigns.

Collaborated with scientists and research assistants in the analysis of ozone depletion and recovery during the seasonal Antarctic ozone hole phenomena by executing detailed scientific literature reviews and assessing mass balance and kinetic computations.

Supported the development of a synthetic blood substitute by analyzing the stability of candidate emulsions in human blood through Near Infrared Spectroscopy and testing different surfactants.

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Achieved high student satisfaction (95%+ in surveys) as a teaching assistant in multiple courses (Environmental Modeling, Differential Calculus, Integral Calculus, etc.) through carefully preparing 3+ hours of weekly lectures/labs/field sessions, providing insightful feedback in the grading of tests and assignments, and conducting a detailed review of exam solutions with my students.

positions.title: Co-Director and Sporting Events Manager
positions.description:
• Planned and directed the sporting events area
• Coached the cycling practices and collaborated in biomechanical research

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description: •	Assisted in the development of nanosensors for uranium in water by performing molecular dynamics simulations to analyze the behavior and stability of uranyl in water using ab initio modified force fields, introducing non-bonded interaction parameters for the water-uranyl intermolecular force field, and obtaining atomic charges using density functional theory.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description:
• Performed a commercial study on the market and uses of coal in Colombia.
• Consolidated market research to find potential customers for the Management of Natural Gas sector.
• Optimized the daily delivery of natural gas with linear programming.
• Reviewed the existing natural gas selling contracts for the audits.
• Uploaded business-existing contracts for natural gas in Ecopetrol’s new pricing system.

positions.title: Farmer
positions.description: • Created a 140m2 crop of alstroemeria flowers in collaboration with Gustavo Montero and Isabel Jeangros on the farm 'La Estancia'.
